cards.name: Divide
cards.summary: Divides the colour underneath by the layer's colour, channel by channel: white in the layer changes nothing, darker values brighten the image, and a 0 channel blows that channel to full. On the blend plate the photo is unchanged under the white bar and pure white under the black bar, and each colour bar blows the channels it lacks to full (lavender under yellow, orange-red under cyan, pink-magenta under green, lime green under magenta, pale cyan under red, yellow under blue); the grey ramp blows the photo to white at its dark end and leaves it nearly unchanged at the light end; the bottom band turns the photo lime green at the opaque magenta end, fading out, and the white type stays white.
use_for: neutralise a colour cast: fill a layer with the cast colour sampled from something that should be white or grey, set it to Divide
clean a scan or phone photo of a drawing: Divide by a heavily blurred copy to turn uneven paper white and keep the lines
flat-field / vignette correction: Divide by a blurred copy of an evenly lit reference
neon, over-bright colour experiments for posters
avoid: Dark or saturated blend colours push channels to 255 at once and the image clips to flat neon; lower Opacity or use a lighter blend colour, or use Curves / Levels for a controlled brighten.
For a soft lift use Screen or Color Dodge at low opacity instead.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.
cards.equivalents_note: No Illustrator blend mode divides. CorelDRAW: Transparency tool > Uniform Transparency, Merge mode Divide (cdrMergeDivide, 10) (script: shape.Transparency.MergeMode); CorelDRAW's merge maths can differ, check the result.
pairs_with: Solid Color fill layer sampled with the eyedropper
Gaussian Blur on a duplicate layer (blurred divisor)
Opacity and Fill sliders in the Layers panel (tame the mode)
Blend If sliders (Layer Style > Blending Options)
layer mask or clipping mask to limit where it acts

cards.name: Exclusion
cards.summary: A softer Difference: white in the layer inverts what is underneath, black leaves it unchanged and 50% grey flattens it to 50% grey, so colours partly invert with low contrast. On the blend plate the bar band looks the same as in Difference (with pure 0 / 100% bar colours the two formulas agree): a blue-tinted negative under white, partial negatives under the colour bars and the plain photo under black; the grey ramp runs from the plain photo through a flat 50% grey at its centre to a low-contrast blue-grey negative at the light end; the bottom band turns the photo violet at the opaque magenta end, fading out, and the white type turns green.
use_for: psychedelic or solarised poster treatments that are softer than Difference
partial colour inversion of a background behind type
avoid: Flattens contrast toward grey in the mid-tones; for a punchier inversion use Difference.
Not for alignment or change checks: identical pixels do not go black (mid-tones come out grey), so use Difference, which turns identical pixels black.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.
cards.equivalents_note: CorelDRAW: Transparency tool > Uniform Transparency, Merge mode Exclusion (cdrMergeExclusion, 36) (script: shape.Transparency.MergeMode).
pairs_with: Gradient Map or Solid Color fill layer as the blend layer
Opacity and Fill sliders in the Layers panel (tame the mode)
Blend If sliders (Layer Style > Blending Options)

cards.name: Hard Light
cards.summary: Multiplies or screens depending on the layer's colour, like a harsh spotlight: layer values lighter than 50% grey screen (lighten), darker ones multiply (darken), 50% grey is neutral, and a layer channel at 0 or 100% forces that channel to 0 or full. On the blend plate the bar band is indistinguishable from Normal, because every bar channel is 0 or 100%; the grey ramp turns the photo into a brightness ramp, near black at the left, the photo itself at the centre and near white at the right; the bottom band is almost flat magenta at the opaque left end, fading to the photo, and the white type takes a pink-magenta tint.
use_for: strong dodge and burn on a 50% grey layer (harsher than Overlay or Soft Light)
High Pass sharpening layer with a crisp, contrasty result
harsh coloured light, texture or grunge overlays that must dominate the image
avoid: Saturated or near-black / near-white layers mostly replace the image; for a gentler blend use Overlay or Soft Light.
Contrast boost clips shadows and highlights quickly; reduce Opacity.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.

cards.name: Hard Mix
cards.summary: Adds the layer's channel values to the image's and snaps each channel to 0 or 255, so every opaque pixel becomes one of eight flat colours (black, white, red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow in RGB). On the blend plate the bar band is indistinguishable from Normal (the bar channels are already 0 or 100%); the grey ramp posterises the photo into flat black, red, yellow and white shapes, black at the dark end and white at the light end; the bottom band goes flat red at the opaque magenta end and breaks into flat red, blue and magenta shapes before fading to the photo; the white type stays white. Partial transparency does not act like plain opacity in this mode: in the half-clear right half of the bottom band the red channel comes out about 10-20 levels lighter than alpha-compositing the snapped result predicts.
use_for: screen-print, pop-art or posterised graphic treatments
hard threshold-style colour separations for stickers and stencils
with Fill (not Opacity) lowered: a strong, smoother contrast and saturation punch
avoid: Full-strength result is extremely harsh and loses all tone; lower Fill rather than Opacity to soften it (Hard Mix is one of the modes where Fill and Opacity behave differently).
For a controllable posterise use Image > Adjustments > Posterize or Threshold instead.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.
cards.equivalents_note: Illustrator's Effect > Pathfinder > Hard Mix is a different operation (keeps the highest CMYK component of overlapping vector fills), not this posterising blend; CorelDRAW has no merge mode that snaps channels to 0 / 255.
pairs_with: Fill slider (softer, contrast-boost version)
Posterize or Threshold adjustment layers
Gradient Map for recolouring after
Opacity and Fill sliders in the Layers panel (tame the mode)
Blend If sliders (Layer Style > Blending Options)

cards.name: Hue
cards.summary: Keeps the luminance and saturation of the image underneath and takes only the hue from the layer, so coloured areas change colour while greys, black and white underneath do not; a neutral (white, grey or black) layer has no hue to give, so it greys the image out. On the blend plate each colour bar shifts the photo to its own hue at the photo's muted saturation (olive, teal, green, mauve-magenta, brick red, periwinkle), while the white and black bars and the whole grey-ramp band leave the photo a plain greyscale image; the bottom band turns the photo and the colour blocks under it magenta at the opaque left end, fading out to the right; the white type stays white.
use_for: recolour a product, garment or prop while keeping its shading and its own saturation
unify mixed-colour elements into one hue family for a campaign look
avoid: Does nothing on neutral greys, black or white; to colour a greyscale image use Color mode.
Pastel areas stay pastel and vivid areas stay vivid; for full control of hue, saturation and lightness use a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.

cards.name: Lighten
cards.summary: Keeps, channel by channel, whichever is lighter of the image and the layer: pixels darker than the layer are replaced, lighter ones stay, and a black layer changes nothing. On the blend plate the white bar is white, each colour bar fills its full channels so the photo shows through tinted pastel (yellow, pale cyan, lime, pink-magenta, orange-red, lavender) and the photo is unchanged under the black bar; in the ramp band the photo shows at the dark end and the ramp's light greys take over toward the white end; the bottom band is near-solid magenta at the opaque left end, fading to the photo, and the white type stays white.
use_for: stack star-trail or light-painting exposures so the brightest light from each frame survives
drop the dark background of fire, sparks or light leaks shot on black (Screen is softer)
remove dark dust specks: a Dust & Scratches copy set to Lighten fixes only dark spots
avoid: Per-channel choice can create a third colour that was in neither layer; to swap whole colours use Lighter Color.
Washes out contrast where the layer is lighter; for a natural brighten use Screen.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.

cards.name: Lighter Color
cards.summary: Compares the luminance (perceived brightness, about 0.3 red + 0.59 green + 0.11 blue) of the image and the layer pixel by pixel and shows whichever whole colour is lighter, so it never mixes channels into a new colour; it is not the total of the channel values. On the blend plate the white, yellow and cyan bars stay solid, the green bar breaks into hard-edged patches of green and photo, the magenta bar is a patchwork of magenta and photo, and the photo shows through the red, blue and black bars; in the ramp band the photo shows at the dark end and wherever it is lighter than the ramp, the ramp's flat greys elsewhere; in the bottom band the layer's flat magenta-to-cyan covers the dark photo except its lightest pixels (the white type, the hairlines, the orange and yellow blocks of the colour strip).
use_for: drop a bright element (sky, light, logo) over a darker photo keeping only where it is brighter, without colour mixing
hard-edged light composites where Lighten would create odd colour fringes
avoid: Hard, aliased switching between the two colours; for smooth blends use Lighten or Screen.
With bright saturated blend colours the layer covers almost everything; check the result and lower Opacity.
Over transparent areas there is nothing to blend with, so the layer shows its own colours; put it over content or clip it.
cards.equivalents_note: No exact equivalent: Illustrator's Lighten compares channel by channel (like Photoshop's Lighten), not whole colours; CorelDRAW's If Lighter is the counterpart of Photoshop's Lighten, not of this whole-colour comparison.
